target.title: fix(agents): strip trailing assistant messages after sessions_yield artifact removal
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #109638.

After `sessions_yield`, `stripSessionsYieldArtifacts()` removes aborted assistant messages and yield interrupt custom messages, but leaves trailing regular assistant messages (from pre-yield tool work) intact. When a sub-agent completes and auto-announce tries to inject a continuation message, it fails because the last visible message is an assistant — causing a deadlock.

## Changes

- **`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.sessions-yield.ts`**: Added a second while-loop pass in `stripSessionsYieldArtifacts()` that strips any trailing regular assistant messages remaining after the yield-specific artifacts are removed. Updated `removeTrailingEntries` predicate to match.
- **`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts`**: Added regression test verifying that after stripping a transcript with pre-yield tool work, the last message is a `tool_result` (not an assistant).

## Why this is safe

`stripSessionsYieldArtifacts` is only called inside the yield abort handler (after `waitForSessionsYieldAbortSettle`). It never runs on non-yield sessions. Trailing assistant messages in the yield context are always intermediate tool-calling work — not meaningful final responses.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: After sessions_yield, auto-announce continuation delivery fails with role-continuity error because trailing assistant messages block injection.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node v24.18.0, vitest

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `npx vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts -t "trailing assistant" --reporter=verbose`

**Evidence after fix**: Test passes in both shards (agents-core 55ms, agents-embedded-agent 43ms). Last message after stripping is confirmed to be tool_result role.

**Observed result after fix**: 2 test files passed, 2 tests passed, 8 skipped (non-matching filter).

**What was not tested**: Full end-to-end yield→announce flow (requires live sub-agent spawn + completion cycle, covered by integration environment).

target.title: feat(bedrock): enable prompt caching for Nova models
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #29707. Amazon Nova generation models on Bedrock were still treated as unsupported non-Anthropic models, so OpenClaw forced `cacheRetention: "none"` and never emitted Bedrock `cachePoint` blocks for Nova requests.

## Why This Change Was Made

AWS documents explicit prompt caching support for Amazon Bedrock models, including Nova generation models: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-caching.html

This change teaches the Bedrock provider to recognize Nova Micro, Lite, Pro, Premier, and Nova 2 Lite refs, lets direct Nova requests keep their explicit cache settings, and keeps the existing no-cache fallback for unsupported non-Anthropic Bedrock models. For Nova, `cacheRetention: "long"` emits the default Bedrock cache point without reusing Claude's `ttl: "1h"` field.

Nova eligibility now has a single owner: the Amazon Bedrock provider normalization seam. The provider sets generic runtime compatibility metadata for eligible Nova models, while the shared agent cache-retention path only consumes that capability and contains no Bedrock model IDs or Nova-family matcher.

## User Impact

Users can enable prompt caching for Bedrock Nova text models without hitting the previous runtime no-cache override. Unsupported non-Anthropic Bedrock models, such as Mistral, continue to be protected from unsupported cache metadata.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(heartbeat): suppress fallback after route-matched message tool
target.body:
When heartbeat runs in message-tool-only mode, a successful generic message tool delivery can still be followed by duplicate free-text fallback narration in the same Telegram chat.

Fixes #84217

## Affected surface

- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts`
  - Adds route-matched message tool delivery evidence for heartbeat replies only after the generic message tool sent to the same provider/target/account route.
- `src/auto-reply/reply-payload.ts`
  - Adds internal reply-payload metadata for route-scoped message tool delivery evidence.
- `src/auto-reply/heartbeat-reply-payload.ts`
  - Adds a heartbeat-specific evidence reader.
- `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts`
  - Suppresses free-text fallback only when the reply carries route-scoped message tool delivery evidence.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-payloads.ts`
  - Leaves heartbeat payloads available for heartbeat-specific route evidence instead of dropping them via generic message-tool dedupe first.
- Tests:
  - `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.tool-response.test.ts`
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts`

## Scope

This is a parameter/evidence threading fix. It does not add a config flag, does not change heartbeat scheduling, and does not touch Slack identity, commitment, or channel-specific private paths.

The important semantic boundary is that "generic message tool delivery evidence" is not the same as "has outbound reply content". This PR only marks heartbeat replies when existing message-tool target evidence matches the same delivery route via the existing `resolveMessagingToolPayloadDedupe` route matcher. Global `messagingToolSentTexts` without route targets is intentionally not enough.

After Vincent's thread-route follow-up, I found one extra current-head issue while refreshing proof: generic reply-payload dedupe could drop the matched heartbeat payload before `heartbeat-runner` saw the route evidence. The current head keeps heartbeat payloads out of that generic dedupe layer so the heartbeat-specific suppression path receives the evidence and can still preserve no-route / wrong-topic fallback behavior.

## Prior art

Prior attempt #84273 was closed by contributor due to inability to provide live channel proof. This PR provides expanded source + runtime helper proof, with the helper semantic explicitly distinguishing "generic message tool delivery evidence" from "has outbound reply content" to address the message-delivery risk flagged in #84273.

The key difference from #84273 is route scope: #84273 marked heartbeat payloads after any message-tool send, while this PR only marks a heartbeat payload when committed `messagingToolSentTargets` match the reply route. If the message tool delivered to another route, or only global text evidence exists, heartbeat fallback still sends.

## Current-head P1 follow-up proof

This update addresses the ClawSweeper P1 finding "Suppress same-route fallback even when the text differs" on head `25958135ed2135dede29e716668ac34cfaea8007`.

The same-route heartbeat evidence rule now treats committed route-matched generic `message` tool target evidence as sufficient for a single plain heartbeat fallback payload, even when the fallback text differs from the tool body. Multi-payload heartbeat replies keep the existing text-match guard so unrelated fallback payloads are not suppressed. Rich payloads, media payloads, reasoning, no-route evidence, wrong-route evidence, and wrong-thread/topic evidence remain outside this suppression path.

target.body:
Closes #108976

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users generating an image in a Telegram (or other channel) chat would receive the same photo twice—once from the resumed agent reply that re-attached media, and once from the completion handoff that already owns delivery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Generated-media completion handoffs already own outbound media delivery (durable host-owned media with direct fallback). The success reply instruction previously told the resumed agent to also attach every `MEDIA` path / structured attachment, which creates a second visible delivery of the same artifact when the agent follows that prompt.

The instruction now assigns a single owner: the completion handoff delivers media; the agent may only write a short caption (or `NO_REPLY`). Image, video, and music generation share this lifecycle helper, so the ownership rule applies across those sibling tools without a Telegram-specific branch.

Compatibility: no config, API, or protocol change. Performance: prompt-text only, no extra I/O. Usability: captions remain allowed; images no longer duplicate. Security: no trust-boundary or secret changes.

## User Impact

After `image_generate` (and sibling media generation tools) completes, users receive each generated artifact once, with an optional caption, instead of two identical channel deliveries a few seconds apart.

## Evidence

Focused tests (local macOS):

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/tools/music-generate-background.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/media-generate-background-shared.test.ts
# Test Files  2 passed (2)
# Tests  35 passed (35)
```

Coverage:

- Shared regression `assigns completion-handoff ownership so the agent is not told to re-attach MEDIA` asserts the wake `replyInstruction` names completion-handoff ownership, forbids re-attaching MEDIA lines, and no longer contains the old dual-attach wording.
- Sibling `music-generate-background` expectations now match that same shared ownership contract (completion handoff owns media; agent is caption-only). This aligns the music completion path with image/video under the shared helper and clears the CI failure that still expected `final-reply MEDIA lines`.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: generated media from `image_generate` (and sibling media tools via the shared helper) must be delivered once; completion handoff owns media while the agent may only caption.
- Environment: local macOS OpenClaw checkout; focused Vitest via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.
- Current-main contrast: success reply instruction told the resumed agent to attach every generated media path with final-reply MEDIA lines (or message-tool attachments) while `durableGeneratedMediaHandoff` also carries the same mediaUrls/attachments into host-owned delivery.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. Inspect `buildMediaGenerationReplyInstruction` for status `ok`.
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/media-generate-background-shared.test.ts -t "completion-handoff ownership"`
  3. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/music-generate-background.test.ts src/agents/tools/media-generate-background-shared.test.ts` → 35/35 pass.
- Evidence after fix: ownership regression passes; music sibling expectations assert completion-handoff ownership and forbid MEDIA re-attach; instruction text requires caption-only / NO_REPLY guidance.
- Control check: wake still sets `durableGeneratedMediaHandoff: true` and still includes `mediaUrls` / attachments on the internal event for host delivery evidence; only the agent-facing ownership instruction changed.
- Observed result after fix: completion wake no longer instructs a second media-bearing reply path for image or music (shared helper).
- Live Telegram: still needed for full acceptance (exactly one `sendPhoto` after one image-generation completion, with caption behavior). A prior Mantis Telegram Desktop run on this PR could not capture a faithful generated-media completion sequence (capture infrastructure / skipped before-after; no visual artifacts), so it did not substitute for a successful single-delivery recording. Happy to re-run or supply a redacted recording when a Telegram tenant path is available.

target.title: fix(discord): bound gateway metadata response reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
@
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo` could buffer an unbounded response body via `response.text()` when fetching the Discord `/gateway/bot` metadata endpoint.

## Rebase Note

Rebased onto current main (9ddd988c9) to pick up the rename `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo` → `fetchDiscordGatewayInfoWithTimeout`. The private helper `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo` is now re-exported for direct testing.

## What Changed (vs previous revision)

- **Rebased onto main**: Resolved merge conflicts with the `fetchDiscordGatewayInfoWithTimeout` rename and added test for stalled DNS preflight.
- **Re-exported `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo`**: The function was un-exported during the main rename; re-exported so bounded-read tests can target it directly.
- **Fixed lint**: Added curly braces to `if (res.destroyed) return;` one-liners in the test (eslint `curly`).

## Why This Change Was Made

**Streaming pre-read bound (primary path):** When the response body stream is available, the function now uses `readResponseWithLimit` to enforce the 4 MiB cap **before** buffering — the stream is read in chunks and cancelled on overflow, matching the existing `materializeGuardedResponse` pattern used by `fetchDiscordGatewayMetadataGuarded`.

**Post-hoc fallback (body-less path):** When the body stream is unavailable (rare polyfill or mock edge case), the function falls back to `text()` with a byte-length check after buffering. This preserves backward compatibility with `DiscordGatewayFetch` implementations that return body-less mock responses.

**Non-transient overflow:** Size overflow now throws as non-transient (`transient: false`) so the detail message propagates to callers instead of being swallowed by the generic "fetch failed" wrapper.

## Evidence

### 1. Static / focused tests

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-metadata.test.ts --run: 9/9 passed
```

Tests cover: body-less success, body-less oversized rejection, **real loopback HTTP streaming oversized rejection** (pre-read bound verified), mutation test, guarded fetch bounded reads, DNS stall timeout, and existing metadata/timeout regression tests.

### 2. Standalone real-behavior proof (terminal transcript)

A standalone proof harness (`gateway-metadata-proof.test.ts`) exercises the REAL production function with real Node.js loopback HTTP:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-metadata-proof.test.ts --run --reporter verbose

 RUN  v4.1.9 G:/AI学习/openclaw

stdout | gateway-metadata-proof.test.ts > standalone real-behavior proof > parses under-cap streaming response from a real loopback HTTP server
  [proof] starting real loopback HTTP server (under-cap) ...
  [proof] server listening on 127.0.0.1:62187
  [proof] response status=200 content-length=chunked
  [proof] ✓ parsed: url=wss://gateway.discord.gg/ shards=1
  [proof] ✓ session_start_limit: total=1000 remaining=999 max_concurrency=1
  [proof] server closed

stdout | gateway-metadata-proof.test.ts > standalone real-behavior proof > rejects oversized chunked response at the streaming 4 MiB boundary
  [proof] starting real loopback HTTP server (oversized chunked) ...
  [proof] server listening on 127.0.0.1:62189, streaming 4456448 bytes (4.3 MiB) in 64 KiB chunks
  [proof] fetch resolved, body is streaming (no content-length)
  [proof] calling fetchDiscordGatewayInfo (production fn with streaming pre-read bound) ...
  [proof] ✓ streaming pre-read bound rejected: Failed to get gateway information from Discord: Discord gateway metadata response body too large: 4259797 bytes (limit: 4194304 bytes)
  [proof] server closed

 ✓ standalone real-behavior proof > parses under-cap streaming response from a real loopback HTTP server 205ms
 ✓ standalone real-behavior proof > rejects oversized chunked response at the streaming 4 MiB boundary 73ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

**What this proves:**
- Real Node.js `http.createServer` streams 4.3 MiB of chunked JSON (64 KiB chunks)
- Real Node.js `fetch` connects to loopback TCP
- Production function `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo` receives the real streaming `Response`
- `readResponseWithLimit` reads chunks via `reader.read()` in a bounded loop
- At the 4 MiB boundary: stream is cancelled, `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo` throws non-transient error with `transient: false`
- Error message: `"Discord gateway metadata response body too large: 4259797 bytes (limit: 4194304 bytes)"`

target.title: fix(xai): add handshakeTimeout to TTS stream WebSocket
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

The xAI TTS stream creates `new WebSocket()` without `handshakeTimeout`. The existing `connectTimer` fires after `timeoutMs` and calls `failConnect()`, which **rejects the promise but does not close or terminate the WebSocket** — the underlying TCP connection and its memory remain occupied. The `handshakeTimeout` at the ws library level cleans up the TCP connection when the HTTP→WebSocket upgrade stalls.

The voice bridge was excluded: its `connectTimeout` already calls `ws.terminate()`, which the pinned ws library aborts the active request and destroys the socket even in CONNECTING state.

## Why This Change Was Made

`handshakeTimeout: timeoutMs` (30 s default) — passes the existing timeout parameter to the ws constructor so the library itself enforces the upgrade deadline and releases TCP resources.

## User Impact

Stalled xAI TTS connections now release TCP resources within their configured timeout instead of leaking them until GC. Healthy connections are unaffected.

## Evidence

### Before vs After (controlled stalled WebSocket upgrade)

A TCP server accepts but stalls the upgrade (partial HTTP 101, no terminating `\r\n`):

```json
{"label":"BEFORE (default=0, unlimited)","handshakeTimeoutMs":0,"outcome":"REJECTED","error":"aborted after 5000ms","elapsed_ms":5016}
{"label":"AFTER (5 s)","handshakeTimeoutMs":5000,"outcome":"REJECTED","error":"Opening handshake has timed out","elapsed_ms":5015}
```

- **BEFORE**: `handshakeTimeout=0` → still hanging at 5 s (aborted externally).
- **AFTER**: `"Opening handshake has timed out"` at 5015 ms — terminated within deadline.

### Why only TTS (not voice bridge)

| Function | Existing timeout mechanism | Cleans up TCP? | handshakeTimeout needed? |
|------|------|------|------|
| `xaiTTSStream` | `connectTimer → failConnect()` | **No** — only rejects promise | ✅ Yes |
| `XaiRealtimeVoiceBridge` | `connectTimeout → ws.terminate()` | Yes — terminate() destroys socket | ❌ No (reverted) |

### Focused tests

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/xai/tts.test.ts --run
Test Files  1 passed (1)  Tests  26 passed (26)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/xai/realtime-voice-provider.test.ts --run
Test Files  1 passed (1)  Tests  36 passed (36)
```

- `expect(ws?.handshakeTimeout).toBe(5_000)` — timeoutMs reaches ws constructor.

target.title: [Bug]: plugin metadata conflict can block gateway startup, and plugin repair/reinstall can silently drop plugin config/allowlist causing state drift
target.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On macOS, upgrading an existing npm/Homebrew-style OpenClaw install to `2026.7.1` can leave external plugins in a split-brain state:

1. a legacy plugin install metadata conflict prevents startup migrations from completing, so the gateway refuses readiness
2. `openclaw doctor --fix` does **not** clear it
3. after manual uninstall/reinstall of the conflicting plugin, the gateway can recover, but other external plugins may still have stale install/index state
4. during follow-up repair, a working plugin can silently lose its config entry / allowlist entry / API-key subtree, so the plugin is physically installed and partially loaded, but the capability is unusable until config is manually restored
5. even after successful recovery and a real successful capability call, some status surfaces still report old version drift

This leaves the system operational only after manual intervention across multiple layers (`plugins.entries.*`, `plugins.allow`, plugin reinstall, gateway restart), and the built-in repair flow does not converge state automatically.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed on a long-lived macOS install with external plugins already configured.

Environment before upgrade:
- OpenClaw `2026.6.11`
- macOS arm64
- Homebrew global install under `/opt/homebrew`
- external plugins present: `openclaw-weixin`, `@openclaw/deepseek-provider`, `@openclaw/tavily-plugin`
- web search configured to use `tavily`
- Tavily API key stored under plugin config

Upgrade flow:

1. Upgrade OpenClaw core to `2026.7.1`
2. Ensure Node is compatible (`v24.18.0` in this repro)
3. Run:
   - `openclaw gateway install`
   - `openclaw gateway start`
4. Observe gateway never becomes ready
5. `openclaw gateway status --deep` shows service loaded/running or restarting, but probe fails / port not truly ready
6. Logs show:

```text
OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready.
Left plugin install index in place because shared SQLite state has conflicting plugin install metadata for: openclaw-weixin
Run "openclaw doctor --fix" against the mounted state/config, then restart the container.
```

7. Run `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive`
8. Observe the same plugin install metadata conflict remains; gateway still not ready
9. Manually force-uninstall and reinstall the conflicting plugin:
   - `openclaw plugins uninstall openclaw-weixin --force`
   - `openclaw plugins install @tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin`
   - `openclaw plugins registry --refresh`
   - `openclaw gateway restart`
10. Gateway finally becomes healthy
11. Now inspect other external plugins (`deepseek`, `tavily`): installed files are present on disk, but status/index surfaces still show old versions or disabled state
12. Attempt a real Tavily call:

```bash
openclaw infer web search --provider tavily --limit 3 --query "OpenClaw 2026.7.1 release notes" --json
```

13. It fails with missing credential error, even though Tavily was previously configured:

```text
Error: web_search (tavily) needs a Tavily API key. Set TAVILY_API_KEY in the Gateway environment, or configure plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey.
```

14. Inspect current config vs backup:
   - `tools.web.search.provider` is still `tavily`
   - but `plugins.entries.tavily` is gone
   - and `tavily` is missing from `plugins.allow`
   - backup config still contains the Tavily API key subtree
15. Manually restore the missing config and allowlist entries, restart gateway, rerun the direct search test
16. Tavily search succeeds, but some status surfaces can still report stale install/version drift

### Expected behavior

- A plugin install metadata conflict should not permanently block startup without a supported convergence path.
- `openclaw doctor --fix` should either resolve the conflict or provide a deterministic repair path.
- Manual uninstall/reinstall of one conflicting plugin should not silently remove config/allowlist/credential subtrees for other working plugins.
- If a plugin capability is actually working again, status surfaces should converge and stop reporting stale drift.
- The combined repair path should be idempotent.

### Actual behavior

- Gateway readiness is blocked by a plugin install metadata conflict.
- `doctor --fix` does not converge the state.
- Manual plugin reinstall is required to recover gateway readiness.
- Another plugin (`tavily`) can lose its config entry, allowlist membership, and API-key subtree during the repair sequence.
- After manual config restoration, the capability works again, but some status/index views still report old version drift or disabled state.

### OpenClaw version

2026.7.1

### Operating system

macOS arm64

### Install method

npm/Homebrew global install

### Model

MiniMax-M3 (not material to the bug)

### Provider / routing chain

- `minimax-portal` for agent runs
- `tavily` for managed web search
- `openclaw-weixin` channel configured

### Additional provider/model setup details

- Gateway managed via macOS LaunchAgent
- external plugins involved in the repro: `openclaw-weixin`, `deepseek`, `tavily`
- Tavily was previously configured and functioning before repair

### Logs, screenshots, and evidence

Representative blocking log:

```text
OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready.
- Left plugin install index in place because shared SQLite state has conflicting plugin install metadata for: openclaw-weixin
Run "openclaw doctor --fix" against the mounted state/config, then restart the container.
```

Representative post-repair Tavily failure:

```text
Error: web_search (tavily) needs a Tavily API key. Set TAVILY_API_KEY in the Gateway environment, or configure plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey.
```

Representative successful direct Tavily test only after manual config restoration:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "capability": "web.search",
  "provider": "tavily"
}
```

State observations during recovery:
- `plugins.entries.tavily` missing from current config
- `tavily` missing from `plugins.allow`
- backup config still contained Tavily `webSearch.apiKey`
- direct capability call worked again only after restoring both config entry and allowlist

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw models auth paste-token` and `paste-api-key` accumulated piped stdin without any size limit, allowing arbitrarily large input to buffer in memory before reaching downstream validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `readPipedStdin()` helper now enforces a 1 MiB cap (matching the existing `MATRIX_CLI_RECOVERY_KEY_STDIN_MAX_BYTES` and `CONFIG_PATCH_STDIN_MAX_BYTES` limits). The rejection happens at the stream boundary — during the read loop, not after buffering — so oversized input never reaches auth processing.

The change follows the same buffer-chunk pattern used in the Matrix recovery-key stdin fix (PR #108120): collect `Buffer` chunks, track `totalBytes` per chunk, and throw before the cap is exceeded. Normal TTY and small piped input paths are unchanged.

target.title: feat: let plugin tools yield turns
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin tools can send work to an external interaction surface, but before this change they could only return a normal tool result. The agent loop could then continue in the same turn before the external callback arrived, which races native approval and form-card flows against the eventual user response.

## Why This Is Better Than The Current Behavior

This adds a narrow runtime control request on `AgentToolResult` and exposes `yieldToolResult(...)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/tool-results`. After a plugin tool returns that result, OpenClaw retains the successful tool result and routes through the existing `sessions_yield` turn-handoff path. A later inbound event can then resume the same session.

Control is applied only after the complete `afterToolCall` finalization lifecycle. Hook-added and hook-replaced controls therefore affect the actual runtime action, and runtimes without a control handler fail explicitly instead of silently continuing.

The implementation remains channel-agnostic. Existing tools and plugins are unchanged when they return no `control` field.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can implement native interaction tools, such as approval or form-card prompts, without racing the model loop against the user callback. Existing plugin tools do not need configuration or migration.

## Implementation

- Add `AgentToolResult.control` and the public `yieldToolResult(...)` helper.
- Add a host-owned finalized-result control seam in agent-core.
- Wire embedded OpenClaw sessions to the existing `sessions_yield` lifecycle.
- Preserve result control through normal, deferred-directory, Tool Search, and Code Mode catalog execution paths.
- Reject unsupported finalized controls with an explicit tool error.

## Evidence

### Real external plugin runtime proof

Environment: macOS arm64, Node 22.23.1, rebased on current main.

A standalone external plugin was loaded from its real manifest through `loadOpenClawPlugins`, registered and resolved `proof_ask_user`, imported `yieldToolResult` from the public Plugin SDK entrypoint, and executed through a real `Agent`. The first run yielded; the finalized successful tool result remained in the transcript; a later inbound prompt on the same Agent completed normally.

target.title: fix(elevenlabs): treat blank env API keys as unconfigured
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Whitespace-only `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` / `XI_API_KEY` environment values are truthy strings, so the ElevenLabs providers treated them as real credentials:

- `buildElevenLabsRealtimeTranscriptionProvider().isConfigured` returned `true` when `XI_API_KEY="  "`, so auto-selection could pick the realtime provider and only fail later at connection time.
- `transcribeElevenLabsAudio` skipped its `ElevenLabs API key missing` guard and sent the speech-to-text request with an empty `xi-api-key` header, surfacing as a confusing upstream 401 instead of a clear local configuration error.

## Why This Change Was Made

The config-file key path already normalizes blanks (`normalizeResolvedSecretInputString`), and the profile fallback already trims (`resolveElevenLabsApiKeyWithProfileFallback`). Only the raw env fallbacks bypassed normalization. This routes them (plus the request-level key, matching the merged xAI handling in `realtime-transcription-provider.ts`) through the same shared `normalizeOptionalString` helper so blank values are treated as missing everywhere in this provider.

## Changes

- `extensions/elevenlabs/realtime-transcription-provider.ts`: `isConfigured` and `createSession` resolve the `XI_API_KEY` fallback via `normalizeOptionalString`, so whitespace-only values report unconfigured and session creation fails fast with `ElevenLabs API key missing`.
- `extensions/elevenlabs/media-understanding-provider.ts`: the speech-to-text key resolution normalizes `req.apiKey`, `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, and `XI_API_KEY` with the same helper, so blank values are skipped and env keys are trimmed before being sent.
- Regression tests: whitespace-only env keys are treated as missing in both providers (including asserting no request is sent), and a padded env key is trimmed before use.

## User Impact

Operators with a whitespace-only `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`/`XI_API_KEY` (e.g., a placeholder left in an env file) now get a clear "ElevenLabs API key missing" error and the realtime provider correctly reports itself unconfigured, instead of a request sent with an empty credential that fails upstream. Real keys are unaffected (verified trimmed-to-same-value in tests). No config, migration, or API changes.

## Evidence

- Focused tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/elevenlabs/` — 38/38 passed on Node 22.22.0.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json` — no errors in changed files (only pre-existing `packages/net-policy` errors from a stale local dependency install).
- Targeted `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` passed for the changed files.
- Real HTTP proof below: loopback server + production functions, before/after this patch.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** A whitespace-only `XI_API_KEY` made the realtime provider report configured, and the speech-to-text path sent a real request carrying an empty `xi-api-key` header instead of failing fast locally.

**Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node v22.22.0, production functions imported directly from the changed sources, real `node:http` loopback server as the ElevenLabs API endpoint (`request.allowPrivateNetwork: true` to permit the loopback target). Current head: `446eea15d5535b6f0c64b2dca9c6d01047f43bac`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx /tmp/elk-proof/proof.mts` with `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=""` and `XI_API_KEY="  "` in the environment. The driver starts a real HTTP server, calls `buildElevenLabsRealtimeTranscriptionProvider().isConfigured({ providerConfig: {} })`, then calls the production `transcribeElevenLabsAudio({ buffer, fileName, mime, baseUrl: <loopback>, request: { allowPrivateNetwork: true } })` and reads the server's received-request count and captured `xi-api-key` header back.

**Evidence after fix:** Before the patch (same driver, base revision): `isConfigured (whitespace XI_API_KEY): true`, `transcribeElevenLabsAudio outcome: resolved (request was sent)`, `server received requests: 1`, `captured xi-api-key header: ""`. After the patch: `isConfigured (whitespace XI_API_KEY): false`, `transcribeElevenLabsAudio outcome: threw: ElevenLabs API key missing`, `server received requests: 0`.

**Observed result after fix:** The whitespace-only env key no longer counts as configured, the missing-key error fires locally before any network I/O (the loopback server confirms zero requests), and regression tests confirm a padded real env key (`"  env-key  "`) is trimmed and sent as `env-key`.

**What was not tested:** No live ElevenLabs API calls (no real credential available); the loopback server stands in for the upstream endpoint. The realtime websocket session path was not connected end-to-end with a blank key; its `isConfigured`/`createSession` gates are covered by the new unit tests and the same normalization helper. No UI changes.

## Intentionally out of scope

- Other providers' env credential paths (bedrock was handled in #109680, `packages/ai` env keys in #109691, deepgram in #108565); this PR is scoped to ElevenLabs only.
- The config-file `apiKey` handling, which already normalizes blanks via `normalizeResolvedSecretInputString`.
- `resolveElevenLabsApiKeyWithProfileFallback`, which already trims its env read.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Gmail watch renewal could launch duplicate `gog gmail watch start` commands when a previous periodic renewal was still stalled. This affects both the gateway-managed watcher and `openclaw webhooks gmail run` when the configured renewal interval is shorter than the command's two-minute timeout.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each Gmail watcher lifecycle now admits only one periodic renewal at a time. Later timer ticks are coalesced until the active command settles, while existing retry timing, failure logging, configuration, and process lifecycle behavior remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Operators no longer get overlapping Gmail watch registration commands during slow or stalled renewals. Normal renewals continue on the next interval after the active command settles.

## Evidence

- Focused tests: `src/hooks/gmail-watcher.test.ts` and `src/hooks/gmail-ops.test.ts` — 2 files, 12 tests passed.
- Targeted formatting and lint checks passed for the four changed files.
- Production-lifecycle proof used the real `startGmailWatcher` scheduler and actual child processes. With `renewEveryMinutes: 1`, the first periodic renewal was held for 70 seconds; after 135 seconds exactly two watch-start calls were observed: the initial registration and one renewal. The minute-two tick did not launch a third command.
- An accelerated repeat of the same child-process scenario was captured by the bounded proof runner and produced the same two-call result.
- Fresh open-PR recall found Gmail watcher PRs for delivery mode, OAuth failure handling, secret argv handling, and bind diagnostics, but no PR implementing this single-flight renewal invariant.

target.title: refactor(gateway-client): expose request dispatch boundary
target.body:
Related: #96230

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway-internal callers can observe a request result or a later `accepted` response, but cannot distinguish a failure before the request frame entered the local WebSocket transport from a failure after dispatch. That distinction is required before later restart-recovery work can make conservative retry or refund decisions without guessing from promise settlement.

This is the first independently reviewable dependency extracted from #96230. The original PR remains frozen while its behavior is split into ordered, narrower changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The protocol client is the only layer that owns the synchronous `socket.send(...)` boundary, so this adds an optional `onDispatched` observer immediately after `send` returns successfully and routes it through the existing callback-isolation helper. The package client and high-level `callGateway` wrapper forward the same observer without changing request frames, protocol versions, timeout/abort cleanup, reconnect behavior, or `onAccepted` response semantics.

The observer contract is intentionally narrow: it means the request frame was handed to the local WebSocket transport. It does not mean the Gateway/server accepted or processed the request. The request option type lives in a dedicated small module and is re-exported from the existing protocol-client module, preserving import and structural type compatibility. `GatewayClient` forwards that shared option shape as a unit, then overrides only its normalized `expectFinal` and `timeoutMs` values; this keeps the oversized implementation LOC-neutral without deleting unrelated comments.

This is a root-cause boundary fix: higher layers no longer need to infer whether transport dispatch happened. The gateway-client package is private and the new field is additive and optional. A consumer/test-double sweep covered the package export, OpenClaw facade, SDK transport, accepted-response caller, both affected request stubs, and the node-host bridge. The node-host bridge only forwards `timeoutMs` across its IPC boundary, so later recovery code must use `callGateway` or introduce a separate IPC dispatch acknowledgement rather than assuming this observer is available there.

Out of scope for this PR: Plugin SDK/session-state isolation, recovery persistence, `mainRestartRecovery` admission or ownership, bounded recovery, quarantine, and Doctor repair. In particular, this PR does not write any production recovery state.

## User Impact

There is no direct end-user behavior change. Existing callers behave exactly as before; later recovery PRs can use a precise local transport-dispatch fact instead of broad failure inference.

Risk is limited to an additive observer callback. It is not invoked when WebSocket send throws, observer exceptions are isolated from request settlement, and the callback must not be interpreted as server acceptance.

Focused TDD reproduction before the original implementation:

target.title: fix(memory-lancedb): make table initialization atomic
target.body:
Closes #105680

## What Problem This Solves

The bundled LanceDB memory plugin checked whether the `memories` table existed and then created it in a separate operation. Two OpenClaw processes initializing the same database could both observe the table as absent, race during creation, and fail startup with a duplicate-create error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing fast path for an already-present table, but make the absent-table path use the LanceDB 0.30.0 atomic `existOk` create mode. This keeps concurrency ownership in the database dependency, avoids a filesystem lock that would not fit remote storage URIs, and keeps schema-row cleanup idempotent.

The regression test starts six independent Node processes against one fresh LanceDB directory and requires every process to complete initialization successfully. The same scenario fails against the previous implementation.

LanceDB documents that `existOk: true` suppresses the existing-table error in create mode and ignores the losing caller supplied data: https://lancedb.github.io/lancedb/js/interfaces/CreateTableOptions/

## User Impact

Gateway and worker processes can initialize the same memory-lancedb store concurrently without intermittent duplicate-create startup failures.

## Evidence

Final-head validation:

- Candidate head: `4e1bc84e3e1`; rebased onto `origin/main` at `652266b8b6c`.
- Production diff after the current TypeScript LOC ratchet: `12 additions / 13 deletions`; the legacy production file no longer grows.

### Standalone concurrent-process behavior proof

Environment: macOS arm64, Node 24.15.0, exact `@lancedb/lancedb@0.30.0`, one fresh temporary local LanceDB directory. This proof ran outside Vitest. The temporary driver started six independent Node processes; each imported the production `extensions/memory-lancedb/index.ts` module and called `testing.createMemoryDb(dbPath, 4).count()`.

Pre-fix control: the same final-head snapshot with only `{ existOk: true }` removed while retaining the test access hook:

```text

initializer 4: failed (1)
```

The final table is usable, all six initializers return successfully, and the temporary schema row is removed.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
